citations.claim: post-collision speed increased despite e<1, showing energy injection
energy exceeds allowed 547.36 at first violating step

counterfactual.change: Reduced restitution e from 0.936 to 0.1 (single field change). With lower e, collision dissipates enough energy to offset spurious gain, so energy drops to 52.8 and no violation, confirming the excess comes from the collision impulse scaling with e / normal handling.

explanation:
Body launched upward into underside of thin horizontal wall (y=2.8,h=0.3). At step 3 body approaches wall, distance to surface 0.15. At step 4 collision resolves but injects energy: speed 30.8 ->33.29, energy 493->573 exceeding E0+10%+5J. Likely wall collision impulse / positional correction using wrong normal or double-counting for thin axis-aligned wall, causing velocity gain, especially in tangential (x) component flipping 11.2 to -24.9.
Ledger: open: wall underside collision energy injection; ruled out: gravity/controller (controller disabled, gravity constant), high dt (dt ~0.009 normal).
vision_note: A blue circular body rises from below toward the left tip of a thin horizontal grey wall over steps 1-3 and makes contact at its underside corner. At step 4 the body visibly overlaps and appears to snag on the wall edge instead of cleanly rebounding, implying a collision-handling anomaly at that instant.
